# 2026: five state elections, five different outcomes

.figwide[<img src="pics/analysis/01_results_2026.png">]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern preliminary results.</div>


---
class: inverse, center, middle

<span class="section-no">1</span>

# The centre is not cracking.
<html><div style='float:left'></div><hr color='#EB811B' size=1px style="width:1000px; margin:auto;"/></html>


---
# CDU/CSU and SPD have been losing ground since the 1980s

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/01_centre_share.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Combined share: West <b style="color:#cc0065">89%</b> in the 1970s → <b style="color:#cc0065">54%</b> in the 2020s
- East: <b style="color:#cc0065">68%</b> in the 1990s → <b style="color:#cc0065">39%</b> today
- 1955–2015: the largest party at <b style="color:#cc0065">all 193</b> state elections was CDU/CSU or SPD. Since 2016: <b style="color:#cc0065">8 of 38</b> went elsewhere
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation.</div>


---
# State parliaments are more fragmented than ever

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/01_fragmentation_enp.png">]

.formula[
<b>Effective number of parties</b> (Laakso & Taagepera 1979)

$$N = \frac{1}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} s_i^2}$$

where $s_i$ is party $i$'s share of seats
]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Around <b style="color:#cc0065">2.2</b> in the West of the 1970s
- <b style="color:#cc0065">3.5 to 4.7</b> in the parliaments elected in 2026
- But: <b style="color:#cc0065">shrinking as AfD becomes dominant</b> in the East, FDP drops out
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation.</div>


---
class: inverse, center, middle

<span class="section-no">2</span>

# The far right is not a new kid on the block.
<html><div style='float:left'></div><hr color='#EB811B' size=1px style="width:1000px; margin:auto;"/></html>


---
# The far right in state parliaments is not new ...

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/02_far_right_timeline.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- NPD in <b style="color:#cc0065">seven Landtage at once</b> in 1968–70
- DVU, REP and Schill in the 1990s and 2000s, mostly for a single term
- The AfD since 2014: <b style="color:#cc0065">all 16</b> states
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation. Bremen: DVU/BIW seats via the separate Bremerhaven threshold.</div>


---
# ... but the AfD is a different animal

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/02_far_right_strength.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Before the AfD: <b style="color:#cc0065">34</b> entries, average <b style="color:#cc0065">6.7%</b>, best 19.4% (Schill, Hamburg 2001), only <b style="color:#cc0065">1 in 3</b> re-elected
- The AfD: <b style="color:#cc0065">41</b> entries, average <b style="color:#cc0065">15%</b>, <b style="color:#cc0065">9 in 10</b> re-elected, always stronger
- 2026: <b style="color:#cc0065">47%</b> of seats in Saxony-Anhalt, 45% in MV
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation.</div>


---
# The recent AfD surge is smaller than it looks

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/02_afd_vs_btw25.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Against the previous state election: <b style="color:#cc0065">+23</b>, +21.5 and +7 points in the September elections
- Against the February 2025 federal result in the same state: <b style="color:#cc0065">+6.7</b>, +3.2 and +1.1
- In the March elections the AfD even <b style="color:#cc0065">underperformed</b> its federal result
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, <a href="https://www.bundeswahlleiterin.de/bundestagswahlen/2025/ergebnisse.html">Bundeswahlleiterin</a>, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/nilssteiner.bsky.social/post/3mvy5n3azt22p">Nils Steiner</a>.</div>


---
class: inverse, center, middle

<span class="section-no">3</span>

# Age, education, and geography are defining cleavages.
<html><div style='float:left'></div><hr color='#EB811B' size=1px style="width:1000px; margin:auto;"/></html>


---
# Support for the centre is dying out

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/03_age.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- CDU under 25: <b style="color:#cc0065">5%</b> in Saxony-Anhalt, <b style="color:#cc0065">1%</b> in MV; the SPD's best group is the over-70s
- The AfD peaks at <b style="color:#cc0065">35–59</b> everywhere and is weakest among the oldest
- Berlin under 35: <b style="color:#cc0065">43–49%</b> Die Linke
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.kas.de/de/monitor-wahl-und-sozialforschung">infratest dimap exit polls, via KAS Wahlanalysen</a>, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://www.zeit.de/politik/deutschland/2026-09/wahlverhalten-junge-menschen-ostdeutschland-volksparteien-cdu-spd">Thorsten Faas</a>.</div>


---
# The AfD's steep education gradient

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/03_education.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- AfD by education (low / medium / high): <b style="color:#cc0065">57 / 52 / 30</b> in Saxony-Anhalt, 46 / 47 / 25 in MV, 26 / 28 / 10 in Berlin
- The Linke and Greens run the other way
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.kas.de/de/monitor-wahl-und-sozialforschung">infratest dimap exit polls, via KAS Wahlanalysen</a>, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/tabouchadi.bsky.social/post/3mvy3gz4vfc2w">Tarik Abou-Chadi</a>.</div>


---
# Village vs. city: the AfD vote falls with municipality size

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/03_urban_rural_afd_by_size.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Village-to-city gap: <b style="color:#cc0065">16–24 points</b> in the East, <b style="color:#cc0065">7–10</b> in the West
- Saxony-Anhalt: 51% in villages under 2,000, 31% in the big cities
- Only the AfD has this gradient; Greens and Linke are its mirror image
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.german-elections.com/">GERDA</a>, <a href="https://wahlen.mvnet.de/wahl/land">Landeswahlleitung MV</a>, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://juliuskoelzer.de/saxony-anhalt-2026-en/">Julius Kölzer</a>.</div>


---
# Berlin: “The Ring is the new Wall”

.fig.sq[<img src="pics/analysis/03_berlin_map.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Left bloc inside the S-Bahn-Ring: <b style="color:#cc0065">67%</b> East, <b style="color:#cc0065">68%</b> West. Outside: 45% East, 47% West
- The AfD still carries the old border: 25% East outside, 16% West outside
- The CDU remains strong in the South-West and North-West
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlen-berlin.de/wahlen/BE2026/AFSPRAES/agh/downloads.html">Landeswahlleiterin Berlin / AfS Berlin-Brandenburg</a>, <a href="https://gdi.berlin.de/">gdi.berlin.de</a>, OpenStreetMap, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://interaktiv.tagesspiegel.de/lab/der-berliner-mamdani-effekt-jung-migrantisch-zentrumsnah-wo-die-linke-stark-geworden-ist/">Tagesspiegel / Julius Kölzer</a>.</div>

---
# Berlin: “The Ring is the new Wall”

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/03_berlin_ring.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- Left bloc inside the S-Bahn-Ring: <b style="color:#cc0065">67%</b> East, <b style="color:#cc0065">68%</b> West. Outside: 45% East, 47% West
- The AfD still carries the old border: 25% East outside, 16% West outside
- The CDU remains strong in the South-West and North-West
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlen-berlin.de/wahlen/BE2026/AFSPRAES/agh/downloads.html">Landeswahlleiterin Berlin / AfS Berlin-Brandenburg</a>, <a href="https://gdi.berlin.de/">gdi.berlin.de</a>, OpenStreetMap, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://interaktiv.tagesspiegel.de/lab/der-berliner-mamdani-effekt-jung-migrantisch-zentrumsnah-wo-die-linke-stark-geworden-ist/">Tagesspiegel / Julius Kölzer</a>.</div>

class: inverse, center, middle

<span class="section-no">4</span>

# Turnout is back.
<html><div style='float:left'></div><hr color='#EB811B' size=1px style="width:1000px; margin:auto;"/></html>


---
# Turnout is back. The East now votes more than the West.

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/04_turnout.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- East German turnout fell to the low 50s in the 2000s and 2010s
- 2026: <b style="color:#cc0065">78%</b> in MV and Saxony-Anhalt, 74% in Berlin
- Saxony-Anhalt: <b style="color:#cc0065">+17.5</b> points, the largest increase at any state election since 1990
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://juliuskoelzer.de/saxony-anhalt-2026-en/">Julius Kölzer</a>.</div>


---
# ... and the new voters went mostly one way

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/04_nonvoter_flows.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- S-A: AfD <b style="color:#cc0065">+170k</b> from former non-voters, all other parties together +96k
- Berlin is the exception: the Linke mobilised more (+75k) than the AfD (+61k)
- Centre and left mostly <b style="color:#cc0065">trade votes among themselves</b>; the AfD also takes from the CDU (−83k, −60k, −32k)
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.kas.de/de/monitor-wahl-und-sozialforschung">ARD / infratest dimap vote-flow analysis, via KAS Wahlanalysen</a>, own compilation. Inspired by: <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/juliusk.bsky.social/post/3mvz7smwnb22e">Julius Kölzer</a>.</div>


---
# ... and they are probably not going away any time soon

.fig[<img src="pics/analysis/04_turnout_persistence.png">]

.notes[
<div class="ta">Take-aways</div>

- 226 state-election pairs since 1946: only about <b style="color:#cc0065">one sixth</b> of a turnout surge is given back next time
- Every East German surge since 2014 was followed by a <b style="color:#cc0065">further rise</b>
- Voting is habit-forming: <b style="color:#cc0065">+5 to +15</b> points next time, strongest for first-time voters
]

<div class="src">Data: <a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a>, own compilation. Literature: <a href="https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/ajps.12210">Coppock & Green 2016</a>, <a href="https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/app.20140533">Fujiwara, Meng & Vogl 2016</a>, <a href="https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-658-42694-1_4">Schäfer 2023</a>.</div>

# Do your own research! The data are at your disposal

<div class="panels">
<div class="panel"><a href="https://www.german-elections.com/"><img src="pics/sources/gerda.jpg"></a><a href="https://www.german-elections.com/">GERDA</a><br><span>municipality- and constituency-level results 1946–2026, R package <code>gerda</code></span></div>
<div class="panel"><a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/"><img src="pics/sources/wahlrecht.jpg"></a><a href="https://www.wahlrecht.de/ergebnisse/">wahlrecht.de</a><br><span>every state election since 1946, all parties, seats, turnout</span></div>
<div class="panel"><a href="https://github.com/zweitstimme-org/polling-api"><img src="pics/sources/zweitstimme-polling-api.png"></a><a href="https://github.com/zweitstimme-org/polling-api">zweitstimme polling API</a><br><span>polls, forecasts and scenarios for federal and state elections</span></div>
